doc.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021

title: Accompanying singers and Roseanna Vitro
summary: As musical director for Roseanna Vitro he did a Randy Newman record nominated for a Grammy; accompanying a singer is an art, with charts and keys.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: What about playing behind singers? © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

Very important and that I still do. I still play the — I’m like the musical director for Roseanna Vitro. And there was one record we did, the music of Randy Newman, and that was nominated for a Grammy. And so playing behind a singer is something very specific. You can’t get in the way of the singer — of the vocal. And you’ve got to know what to do with that.
Yeah that’s a whole other class in itself. You could have a vocal accompaniment class it seems to me.
Yes. It’s a whole art form. It’s an art form to play behind a singer. Yup.
I find it’s tricky when you're playing behind a singer and all you have are chord charts.
Because if you don’t know what the melody is, how are you going to keep out of the way of the melody unless you know it.
Well hopefully the vocalist will write in the chart the melody so, you know, that’s very very important.
Yeah. Have you ever had a singer say can I sing with you and you go sure, and they’ll mention a song and you go what key and they go, “Well my first note is [hums]”?
Well hopefully I’ll grab it from that. I mean you know not all the time does that happen but, it can happen.
